page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin holds three marginal notes: "Hordeū." beside the first lines, "Hordeū munda- tum. N." beside the middle lines, and "Frumen- ta omnia pro cœli statu va- riant." beside the lower middle lines. No right margin text. Below the text, at the foot right, a catchword.

main_text.p: Hordeū. Hordeum ad varios medicinæ vsus vsur- patum ab antiquitus inuenitur, & nobilissimum ab iis frumentum appellatum est. Hodie raro lautiorum atq; magnatum mensas subit, nisi cortice suo castratum, Hordeū munda- tum. N. mundatum bordeum ap- pellatum, rundendo enim deglubitur, oder geschelte Gersten / elixum enim primo cibo iuxta solet, stomacho non ingratum præfer- tim si aceti modicum fuerit permixtum: quod si vero diu satiue elixum non fuerit, inflat, & ventriculo noxium est, minus enim abstergit. Plurimum eo in papatu vescuntur in ieiunio illo quadragenario. Caeterum cum bordeum cuiq; notissimum sit, hic illud delineare opera pretium est, Frumen- ta omnia pro cœli statu va- riant. quod si, aut in alijs, mini sse & hic oportet, omnia fœmina, præcipue vero frumenta pro locorum natura varia, cœlo, statu in quo fata sunt & ænatæ, boni tatem adipisci vel malignitatem. Maturius feriētur quam triticum, & primo ex omnibus fru- mentis erumpit à primo satu, die vt plurimum septimo, magis, festinat quam triticum. In Ægypto sertio quarto sue dieprovenit, sexto verò à satu mense metitur, in Hellade septimo, in Peloponneso ostauo, Æthiopes non aliam quam mili & bordei frugem nouerunt. Melius autem deteriùs, fit cultura & foli natura. Terram requirit optimam & bene stercoratam, quæ sit destituitur, facile in lolium transit & degene- rat præsertim pluuio sa tempestate. Causam hujus

page.notes: Page is faded and partly blurred at the lower right; the last line reads "hujus" only as a best guess. Several words in the first lines and in the marginal notes are doubtful, notably "antiquitus", "fata", "oder geschelte Gersten" and the Greek-derived names (Ægypto, Hellade, Peloponneso, Æthiopes). Heavily marked words are reconstructions from the faint scan and are not certain. The catchword and the "hujus" ending are uncertain. The black-letter phrase is taken as German inside roman text.
